\section{Acknowledgements}

I would like to express my gratitude to Kuniaki Konishi for supporting this internship at The University of Tokyo. He trusted me and helped me with feedback as well as with the preparation of this report.
I also want to express my gratitude to Kimura Wataru for helping me understand the experiment and for allowing me to interact with it (installation of a delay line). I would also like to thank Adelin Patoux for teaching me how to use Tidy3D (FDTD software). I would like to thank the University of Tokyo International Office for helping me with the visa and many paperwork. They have been a precious help in properly setting up in Tokyo. I would also like to thank Sorbonne University's administration services, such as Delphine Robar (iMAT) and Aurore Monflier (Help for Mobility), for the international mobility grant. Also, Massimiliano Marangolo for supporting my record.
I want to also thank the Sorbonne's Master's administration, Valérie Boillevin, and Odette Combrisson for the help during this year and the previous ones. I also thank the Master QuOM and PFA for the precious teachings and insightful courses.

Since this is the end of the master, I would like to thank many people involved in this successful academic trail that started very badly eight years ago, when I freshly registered into Sorbonne University while having to face a bone cancer. I would like to thank Xavier Michaut for having assisted me in integrating CMI Physique despite the situation and for following me up during this time. I also thank many doctors and physiotherapists that literally helped me not to die before my 20th. This includes the GOAT of orthopedic surgery, Prof. David Biau, who performed a new operation procedure on me that not only was successful but also allowed me to walk again and not lose my leg. Actually, his work has been so excellent that I succeeded in the ascent of Mont Fuji, something that was impossible to even think about many years ago.

I also warmly thank Dr. Pascaline Boudou-Rouquette for her long-time follow-up of my case and her all-time support along these eight years. I also thank Dr. Ludovic Fournel for his two lung surgeries that also helped me not to die.
I also thank many physiotherapists for having carried out all the work to help me walk again, but also for helping me not to despair when things were pretty grim. I also thank all the nurses and doctors of A.P.H.P Cochin and Clinique Edouard Rist for their support.
I would like to also thank many people at Sorbonne University, such as Steve Zozio for the administrative support during the bachelor's and my mobility in Switzerland, Pauline Yzombard for the support during the master's, and my many professors who were essential in building up this academic background. I would like to thank Prof. Jérôme Beugnon and Prof. Sophie Trincaz-Duvoid for their support with recommendation letters. I would like to express my gratitude to Prof. Marie D'Angelo for her support for my internships in Japan.

I also want to thank all of my internship supervisors who trusted me and helped me build up an interesting experience in laboratories. This includes Prof. Emily Lamour for my internship at INSP, Prof. Matthieu Delbecq at LPENS, Prof. Carole Diederichs also at LPENS, Prof. Kazuyuki Sakamoto at Osaka University, and of course Prof. Kuniaki Konishi at the University of Tokyo.

I want to thank Minami Fujioka for her support in Japan. I also want to thank all my friends who supported me during all those difficult years, coming to the hospital, helping me rebuild a normal life despite many circumstances (cancer, COVID, etc.). I want to also thank my family for their unwavering support. This academic success is the result of the work of so many people for so many years, but also of my relentless will to pursue my life.

To quote Snoop Dogg: "Last but not least, I want to thank me. I want to thank me for believing in me. I want to thank me for doing all this hard work. [...] I want to thank me for never quitting."
To conclude more seriously, I am grateful to have carried out all of those experiences and ended up where I wanted to be, to have been able to know myself better.
